title: How the upload service moves a photo
subtitle: Five parts, six connections, and what happens when one of them has a bad day

nodes.label: Upload API
nodes.simple: The front door. It checks the upload, stores its record and hands the heavy work to the queue.
nodes.deep: A stateless HTTP service. It validates size and type, writes one metadata row, publishes one job and answers 202 without waiting for any thumbnail.
nodes.owns: Upload ids and the first metadata row of every upload.
nodes.runs: Container pool behind the public load balancer.
nodes.scale: Horizontally, add containers. Tops out at the store connection limit.

nodes.label: Job queue
nodes.simple: A waiting line for thumbnail jobs, so a burst of uploads never overwhelms the workers.
nodes.deep: A durable queue with acknowledgements. A job stays in the queue until a worker acknowledges it, so a crashed worker means a redelivery, never a lost job.
nodes.owns: Pending thumbnail jobs and their delivery order.
nodes.runs: Three-node cluster in the private subnet.
nodes.scale: Add partitions. A single partition tops out near one consumer group.

nodes.label: Thumbnail worker
nodes.simple: Takes one job at a time, makes the small versions of the photo and records the result.
nodes.deep: Pulls a job, reads the original, renders three sizes, writes them and the rows that point at them, then acknowledges the job and asks the CDN to forget old copies.
nodes.owns: The thumbnail files and the rows that list them.
nodes.runs: Autoscaled batch pool, no public address.
nodes.scale: Add workers until the queue drains. CPU bound, so about one per core.

nodes.label: Photo store
nodes.simple: The one place that remembers every upload and where its files live.
nodes.deep: A relational database with one primary and a replica. It is the source of truth for upload status, and the CDN pulls originals from it.
nodes.owns: Upload status and the list of files for each photo.
nodes.exposes: SQL over TLS, plus an object read endpoint for the CDN.
nodes.scale: Vertically for writes, read replicas for reads. Tops out near 2,000 writes a second.

nodes.label: CDN
nodes.simple: Keeps copies of popular images close to viewers so most reads never reach the store.

traces.title: Upload a photo
traces.trigger: A user taps Upload in the app.

steps.title: Accept the upload
steps.simple: The API checks the file and answers right away with an id, before any thumbnail exists.
steps.deep: Size and type are validated, one row is written with status received, one job is published, and the client gets 202 with the upload id.

code.src:
def accept(upload):
    row = db.insert(upload.meta, status="received")
    queue.publish(job(row.id))
    return 202, row.id

steps.title: Park a job
steps.simple: The queue holds the job until a worker is free.

steps.title: Make the thumbnails
steps.simple: A worker renders three sizes of the photo.
steps.deep: The worker reads the original, renders 128, 512 and 1024 pixel versions and keeps them in memory until the write.

steps.title: Record the result
steps.simple: The store marks the upload ready and lists its three files.

traces.title: Read a cold image
traces.trigger: A browser asks the CDN for an image it has not cached yet.

steps.title: The CDN misses its cache
steps.simple: The CDN has no copy, so it asks the store for the original.

steps.title: The store serves the original
steps.simple: The store answers the read and the CDN gets the bytes.

steps.title: The CDN keeps a copy
steps.simple: The next viewer is served straight from the cache.

invariants.breaks: Two writers race and a reader sees a half-overwritten thumbnail.

invariants.rule: An upload id is accepted at most once.
invariants.breaks: A retried request creates a duplicate row and a duplicate job.

invariants.rule: The store is the source of truth for status.
invariants.breaks: The app shows ready while the files are still missing.

pressure.title: Queue backlog during a burst
pressure.limit: About 5,000 jobs a minute per worker pool.
pressure.signal: Queue depth keeps growing for more than five minutes.
pressure.mitigation: Add workers and cap new uploads per user.

pressure.title: Store write connections
pressure.mitigation: Pool connections in front of the primary.

whatifs.title: The worker crashes mid-job
whatifs.change: A worker process dies after rendering but before it acknowledges the job.
whatifs.outcome: The queue redelivers the job, so the thumbnails are made twice and the store sees a second write.
whatifs.lesson: At-least-once delivery means every consumer must be safe to run twice.

whatifs.title: The queue loses its disk
whatifs.change: The queue cluster restarts with an empty disk.
whatifs.outcome: Every pending job is gone. Uploads stay at received forever and nobody is told.

decisions.title: Thumbnails in the background
decisions.chosen: Answer the upload at once and make thumbnails later through a queue.
decisions.context: Uploads arrive in bursts and thumbnailing takes seconds of CPU per photo.
decisions.consequences: Users briefly see an upload without thumbnails, and the status field must tell the truth.
decisions.simple: The user should not wait for image work.
decisions.deep: Rendering inside the request would tie the API pool to CPU load and turn every burst into timeouts.

alternatives.name: Render in the request
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest, but slow responses and no way to absorb a burst.

alternatives.name: Render on first read
alternatives.tradeoff: No queue, but the first viewer pays and the CDN sees slow origins.

decisions.title: One database for status
decisions.chosen: Keep upload status in the same SQL database as the metadata.
decisions.context: Status and metadata change together and must never disagree.
decisions.consequences: The database is a shared ceiling on write throughput.
decisions.simple: One place to look for the truth.

alternatives.name: Status in the queue
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer writes, but status disappears when a job is acknowledged.

risks.title: Uploads can stay received forever
risks.what: If a job is lost nothing ever marks the upload failed, so the app shows a spinner for good.
risks.fix: Add a sweeper that fails uploads older than ten minutes.

quiz.q: Why does the API answer before any thumbnail exists?
options: Rendering would tie request time to CPU load
quiz.why: Rendering in the request would turn every burst into timeouts, so the work moves behind the queue.

quiz.q: A worker dies before acknowledging a job. What happens next?
options: The queue delivers the job again
quiz.why: Acknowledgement is what removes a job, so an unacknowledged job is redelivered.

quiz.q: Which connection is drawn dashed on the map?
quiz.why: Publishing a job is fire and forget, so the caller does not wait for the reply.

quiz.q: What does the CDN do on a cache miss?
options: Asks the store for the original
Asks the worker to render it
quiz.why: On a miss the CDN pulls the original from the store and keeps a copy for the next viewer.

glossary.def: A delivery promise: every message arrives one or more times, never zero, so duplicates are possible.
Work that has arrived but is not yet done, such as jobs waiting in a queue.
